questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That is was easy to access academically - or in other words compatible with my danish syllabus. Furthermore that I was intrigued by the culture, and the nature of the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy. A lot of information goes unsaid, so when I left I was a bit unsure how it all would go, but upon my arrival, I got confirmed that everything indeed was under control.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A bus from The University of Limerick was waiting for me when I arrived. The reception to my village was also open so I could get the keys to my apartment - I arrived quite late, so this was really nice. I felt well taken care of upon my arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was confused about certain things - like whether to bring bed-linen (I didn't need to so I made the right call luckily)  and other small stuff like that, but all the essential parts were very clear.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are quite a few villages available. I choose Troy Village (which is technically off-campus, but University of Limerick is also involved) because I read here that a lot of other international students also lived there and that it was within a cheaper price range (this was also true when I arrived).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I don't know about meal plans, but there was a reasonable kitchen and some supermarkets close by (Aldi), which made food very easy to access - also quite a few cafes on campus!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is expensive! But this is the general case with Ireland due to the housing crisis, so if you get a place to stay take it!  Also, all the villages are quite similar I would say - what varies is the size of desks and size of beds mostly. Furthermore, I thought that Plassey village was quite nice and could recommend that!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because it is so hard finding accommodation and it is very expensive due to this fact, it is not great, but it is at no fault of the University.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fine! A bit overwhelming but I guess that is the case with every Erasmus stay. Overall okay :)) I found it a bit confusing, but they will write to you if you forget anything, so it's all good.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could mail both the host and home instituaiton. If I remember correctly there was also a booklet of help if you needed it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
They only make the official booklet of modules available to you (where you can see what courses to take) available last minute, so sometimes your pre-approval will not be applicable and you would have to start over with this - this happened to me which was a bit frustrating. But apart from that, there is a lot of nice people willing to help you to the best of their abilities, and they are used to dealing with international/Erasmus students. 
When you are an Erasmus student they will also have two weeks when you arrive before you choose which course you want to take - this is quite convenient as it gives you time to figure everything out before your settle on a module.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When it comes to modules keep your calm. It can be a bit frustrating but it will probably work out!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses at University of Limerick were good, but in general a bit lower than at the University of Copenhagen I would say. I also greatly missed a critical approach as a lot of it was taught as "this is how it is".

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I liked the exams/assignments better here! it was very nice and also manageable for an Erasmus student! Apart from that quite the same, apart from the fact that there isn't as much student participation in the classes at UL.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PS4031 - PSYCHOLOGY AND EVERYDAY LIFE
PS4097 - DEVELOPMENTAL PSYCHOPATHOLOGY
PS4107 - ABNORMAL AND CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY
SO4001 - INTRODUCTION TO SOCIOLOGY
SO4118 - THE SOCIOLOGY OF GENDER AND POPULAR CULTURE

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
SO4118 - THE SOCIOLOGY OF GENDER AND POPULAR CULTURE
This was very good and opened my horizons to great topics - you are able to gain such a nuanced perspective on otherwise polarized debates - truly wonderful!
Can be recommended even though I study psychology and not sociology.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Spend a lot more money on going out (beer - a lot of it) than I expected, but it was very much worth it!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, Ireland was a bit more expensive than I expected - maybe the same or a little lower than in Denmark, but quite close.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was ecelent!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many! it is hard to name them all! UL really has these things nailed down. There were numerous clubs with so many activities of all tastes and weekly trips to Irish attractions all over Ireland. I was also a part of the student ambassador program which was amazing. Really nice all of it. If you want to do something, there is always people down to join you - from knitting to sports!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them! Especially the Student ambassador program if that is possible, and if not the weekly trips - they are very nice!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
In terms of nature: Killarney National park for hikes. The Slea Head Drive for some VERY beautiful nature by car. 
In terms of cities: Adare is nice. Galway is a must! I also heard that Belfast should be amazing. I personally didn't like Dublin that much.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. I was a bit surprised by the 'lad culture' but apart from that, it was quite nice. People are very friendly - and not faced by the cold!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Seek them out :)) I spend most of my time with international students, which I don't regret, but I know some people used online meeting sites such as Bumble to meet locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The 'lad culture' can be a bit intimidating and uncomfortable at times. Apart from that, it was really nice!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are so kind and welcoming! I also enjoy the small talk a lot!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Rainwear of course - especially if you want to go for hikes! It rains so much here, that they do all planned activities irrespective of weather.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Limerick has been known as a rough city, but not it is mostly fine. Although be aware of drugging and spiking at nightclubs (I've only heard about it in clubs, but never experienced it myself). And although Limerick is quite safe, it is better to walk home with a friend if it is night.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people. They are so great. It is indescribable. Also, the nature is breathtaking. Really something you have to experience for yourself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with FOMO - there is so much great stuff to do all of the time which I really wanted to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
